mcqs.question: A solid cube of side 10 cm is melted and recast into a sphere. What is the radius of the sphere (in cm)?
mcqs.explanation: When a solid is melted and recast, its volume remains the same. Volume of the cube = 10^3 = 1000 cm³. For a sphere, (4/3)πr³ = 1000 ⇒ r³ = 750/π ≈ 238.73 ⇒ r ≈ 6.2 cm. Options A, C and D arise from incorrect assumptions such as equating surface areas or using side length directly.

mcqs.question: A solid cylinder of radius 3 cm is melted and recast into a sphere of radius 5 cm. What is the height of the original cylinder (in cm)?
mcqs.explanation: Set the volumes equal. Cylinder: V = πr²h = π·9·h = 9πh. Sphere: V = (4/3)π·5³ = (500/3)π. Equating gives 9πh = (500/3)π ⇒ h = 500/(27) ≈ 18.5 cm. Options A, B, D result from arithmetic errors or forgetting to divide by 9.

mcqs.question: A metal block has dimensions 2 m × 30 cm × 0.5 dm. After melting, it is recast into a cube. What is the side length of the cube in centimeters?
mcqs.explanation: Convert all dimensions to cm: 2 m = 200 cm, 30 cm = 30 cm, 0.5 dm = 5 cm. Volume = 200 × 30 × 5 = 30,000 cm³. Cube side = ∛30,000 ≈ 31 cm. Options A, C, D arise from using inconsistent units or mis‑calculating the cube root.

mcqs.question: A cylindrical pipe of radius 7 cm and length 2 m is melted and recast into a solid sphere. What is the radius of the sphere (in cm, correct to two decimal places)?
mcqs.explanation: Convert length to cm: 2 m = 200 cm. Cylinder volume = π·7²·200 = 9800π cm³. Sphere volume = (4/3)πR³ = 9800π ⇒ R³ = 7350 ⇒ R ≈ 19.30 cm. Options A, B, D are results of using wrong formulas or forgetting the 4/3 factor.

mcqs.question: When a solid is melted and recast into another shape, which physical quantity remains unchanged?
mcqs.explanation: Melting and recasting does not add or remove material, so the volume (and consequently the mass) stays the same. In the context of NCERT Class 10, the principle emphasized is volume conservation. Surface area and color can change.

mcqs.question: A cube of side 6 cm is melted and recast into a cuboid of dimensions 4 cm × 3 cm × ? cm. What is the missing dimension?
mcqs.explanation: Volume of cube = 6³ = 216 cm³. Let the missing dimension be x. Then 4 × 3 × x = 216 ⇒ x = 216/12 = 18 cm. Options A, B, D arise from arithmetic slips.

mcqs.question: A solid sphere of radius 5 cm is melted and recast into a cube. Which of the following equations correctly relates the radius r of the sphere to the side a of the cube?
mcqs.explanation: Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³ and volume of cube = a³. Equating them gives (4/3)πr³ = a³. Options B, C, D misuse the formula or mix surface area with volume.

mcqs.question: A rectangular block measures 0.5 m × 20 cm × 5 dm. After melting, it is recast into a sphere. What is the radius of the sphere in centimeters (rounded to one decimal place)?
mcqs.explanation: Convert all dimensions to cm: 0.5 m = 50 cm, 20 cm = 20 cm, 5 dm = 50 cm. Volume = 50 × 20 × 50 = 50,000 cm³. For a sphere, (4/3)πR³ = 50,000 ⇒ R³ = (3·50,000)/(4π) ≈ 11,938.5 ⇒ R ≈ 22.9 cm. Options A, B, D result from unit errors or incorrect cube‑root calculation.
